designThesis.truthTask: A reader compares five digitised lantern-slide records, narrows them by title/series, opens one and returns to the same result context.
decisions: Record plate size is the identity device: each schematic frame's aspect box is set from the supplied catalogue width/height (8.3x8.3, 10x8.3, 8.3x10), and the list thumbs use the same ratios.
Serif record titles against monospace accession/field labels read as a catalogue sheet rather than a photo gallery, because no archival photograph exists to lead with.

Honest evidence limits are structural, not decorative: a persistent scope note in the masthead, an inline caption on every plate, a duplicate notice on LS-19, and a 'what this record does not establish' panel.
designThesis.application: Result context (query, series, result order, scroll, focus) is retained by keeping browse DOM alive and hidden rather than re-rendering on return.

rationale: Standard create workflow, one visual system, no alternatives built because the task structure was settled by the prompt. Priority order was: correct facts and duplicate semantics > context retention and focus return > responsive comparison layout > visual identity. Identity is derived only from supplied metadata (series, medium, declared dates, plate dimensions, condition notes) and from the stated absence of archival imagery; nothing was invented about provenance, photographers, institutions, licences or conservation outcomes.

failuresFound.finding: axe WCAG 2.0/2.1 AA 'label-content-name-mismatch' (serious) on button[data-open=LS-02] and button[data-open=LS-19]
failuresFound.cause: The record button carried an aria-label summary that did not include the visible 'Second copy of LS-02' sub-line, so the visible text was not contained in the accessible name.
failuresFound.fix: Replaced the aria-label override with a visible sr-only 'Open record ' prefix inside the button, letting the accessible name come from the real visible text. Rechecked: 0 axe violations, and the duplicate's warning is now part of its accessible name.
failuresFound.author: creator

failuresFound.finding: Content touched the screen edge at 320 and 390px (browse records and detail panel measured x=0)
failuresFound.cause: #browse and #detail ID-selector padding shorthand (padding: 44px 0 8px) overrode the .wrap horizontal gutters by specificity.
failuresFound.fix: Split into padding-top/padding-bottom so .wrap keeps its 16px/24px side gutters. Rechecked: 16px gutters at 320 and 390, 24px at 1440, scrollWidth equals clientWidth at all three widths.
failuresFound.author: creator

failuresFound.finding: Control border --rule-strong measured 2.72:1 against paper, below the 3:1 non-text contrast guidance for control boundaries
failuresFound.cause: Chosen tone was too light for the warm paper background.
failuresFound.fix: Darkened to #74725F (3.86:1 on paper, 4.43:1 on surface, 4.66:1 on input fill). Affects search border, chip borders, the record-button chevron and section rules. Rechecked by calculation; not re-measured by a dedicated non-text-contrast tool.
failuresFound.author: creator

knownRemainingIssues.issue: At 200% text zoom in a 320px viewport the page overflows horizontally to 441px: the masthead stamp paragraph (max-width 16ch) and the 'Listed in catalogue order' line stay on one line, and the h1 does not reflow below its longest word.
knownRemainingIssues.severity: reflow edge case beyond the requested 320/390/1440 support widths; content still reachable by scrolling.
knownRemainingIssues.status: not fixed — one self-correction pass was already spent; recorded rather than silently dropped.
